clue.text: Moral principles in middle of sixteenth century put down in this

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, and this nine-letter word has exactly one
something put down in a place is set inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the fifth of the nine letters is its centre
taken as written
C is the standard abbreviation for century

explanation.surface: A historian notes that a moral code was laid down in a book in the mid-1500s.
explanation.walkthrough: E comes first, then C goes inside THIS to give ETHICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics is the usual name for a set of moral principles governing conduct.

clue.text: Covering the entire distance, from the beginning

blocks.note: first meaning: over the full length of something
second meaning: throughout, the whole time

explanation.walkthrough: One phrase read literally (along the whole route) and idiomatically (since the start, as in 'I knew it all along').
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both over the whole length and throughout a period of time, an idiom for 'from the start'.

clue.text: Scholar in a goods vehicle in street

indicators.note: placed in a street means sitting between that street's letters

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a van is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: An academic is spotted sitting in a delivery van parked on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, a synonym for scholar.

clue.text: They may be used by a camper, foreign gent with pets

definitions.text: They may be used by a camper

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A camper from abroad arrives with his animals in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent pegs are the spikes a camper drives into the ground to anchor a tent, so the description is an example-style definition.

clue.text: Urge to get prize piece of tableware

blocks.note: to egg on is to urge
a cup is a trophy or prize

explanation.surface: Someone is spurred on to win a valuable item of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cup is a small holder for a boiled egg, an item of tableware.

clue.text: Major duel - one it bothered in play

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed or troubled, so the preceding letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big duel troubles one character in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Apt surface: the play has major duels, Tybalt against Mercutio and then Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of the star-crossed lovers is the play in question.

clue.text: To depart, follow green light

blocks.note: to take a road is to follow it
leave is permission, a green light to go ahead

explanation.surface: A driver is told to set off and go when the traffic lights change.
explanation.definitionFit: To take leave of someone is to say goodbye and go, an idiom for departing.

clue.text: Be an authority on tear-jerkers?

blocks.note: surface reading: be an expert on sentimental films that make audiences weep
setter's reading: the things that make you cry are vegetables you chop, so the expert knows about them in a literal sense

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being expert is taken literally: the 'tear-jerkers' are the vegetables that make eyes water when sliced, not weepy films.
explanation.definitionFit: To know your onions is a British idiom meaning to be an expert in a subject.

clue.text: Good opportunity in school

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
room, as in room for manoeuvre, is scope or opportunity

explanation.surface: A pupil is getting a fine chance at their place of education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun for the place; here it is the verb meaning to train.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or prepare them, which is what grooming a candidate means.

clue.text: Give the wrong impression being crazy about Skye, perhaps

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the crazy word goes round the island

blocks.note: mad means crazy
Skye is a Scottish island, an example of an isle

explanation.surface: Someone gives a false picture by raving about a Scottish holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that Skye is just one example of the category wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead is to deceive or cause someone to believe something untrue.

clue.text: Grand Prix track, circuit in Lima rebuilt

indicators.note: one thing in another sits among that other's letters
something rebuilt is put together again differently, so the combined letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letter O is round like a circuit
taken as written; Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A motor-racing venue is reconstructed in the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuit' looks like part of the definition alongside 'track'; it is only the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Imola is the Italian town whose racing circuit has hosted Formula One Grands Prix.

clue.text: Those who assault strikers?

blocks.note: first meaning: people who make an assault
second meaning: forwards in a football team, whose job is to score

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests workers on strike or people who hit; in football the strikers are the attacking forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, attackers and strikers are both names for the forward players who try to score.

clue.text: Not quick to grasp what the pro is with a golf club?

blocks.note: straight reading: a person who is dim-witted and takes a while to understand

blocks.clueFragment: what the pro is with a golf club?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a golf professional swings the club back up slowly before striking the ball

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is split as 'up take': a golfer's takeaway, lifting the club back, is done deliberately slowly by a pro.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slow on the uptake is an idiom for taking a long time to understand things.

clue.text: Large centrepiece required - English salesman returned with duff gen

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the salesman is read from right to left
duff is British slang for faulty or useless, so the following letters come out in broken order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a rep is a sales representative
taken as written; gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An English sales rep comes back with bad information about a big table display.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental stand with dishes, used as a large decoration in the middle of a dining table.

clue.text: Antelope crossing fine line in enchanted place

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the animal's letters span the pair placed inside

blocks.note: the eland is a large African antelope
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An antelope steps over a thin boundary in a magical land.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfland is the fairy realm of folklore, an enchanted kingdom of elves.

clue.text: A German beer mug for a renowned scientist

blocks.note: ein is German for a
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A drink from a German tankard is offered to a famous physicist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German' looks like a German person; it means the German word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist behind relativity, is the most famous scientist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Home Counties gave up, withdrew

blocks.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: The counties around London surrendered and pulled out of the union.
explanation.definitionFit: A region that secedes formally withdraws from a federation or union.

clue.text: US agency holding a married bloke in Asian country

indicators.note: something holding other things grips them inside itself

blocks.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married
bod is British slang for a person or bloke

explanation.surface: American spies detain a married man somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a country in South-East Asia, bordering Thailand and Vietnam.

clue.text: How a tot in a high chair eats, in poverty?

definitions.text: How a tot in a high chair eats

blocks.clueFragment: How a tot in a high chair eats
blocks.note: first meaning, literal: a toddler picks food up and puts it in its mouth
second meaning, idiomatic: living with nothing to spare

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for scraping by is taken literally as a small child feeding itself with its fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Living from hand to mouth means having only enough money for immediate needs, an idiom for being poor.

clue.text: Some pythons, huge in part of Japan

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the wanted letters are a run taken from within the next words

blocks.note: the run straddles the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Some enormous snakes live in a region of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Honshu is the largest of Japan's main islands, home to Tokyo.

clue.text: Disordered routine, back tender

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the routine is written from its end

blocks.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
a tender is a bid or offer

explanation.surface: A chaotic schedule is followed by a painful return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' suggests sore or gentle; it is the noun meaning a formal offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbid means muddy or confused, and figuratively disordered or in turmoil.

clue.text: Unorthodox religious opinion at this place on the outskirts of Shrewsbury

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: here means at this place
the edge letters of the town name

explanation.surface: A dissenting belief is found here on the edge of a Shropshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrewsbury is the county town of Shropshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is belief contrary to the orthodox doctrine of a church.

clue.text: Sci-fi film in register, reviewed after another

indicators.note: viewed again, as if looking back over it, so the register is read backwards

blocks.note: alien means belonging to another, foreign
a rota is a register or list of duties

explanation.surface: A science-fiction movie appears in a list of films reviewed one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sci-fi film' tempts you to write ALIEN at once; that is only the first part, from 'another'. The register comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienator is a 1990 American science-fiction action film.

clue.text: Willow, very large one about to be cut back?

indicators.note: cut back read as turned back, so this short word runs the other way

blocks.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
I is the Roman numeral one
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A huge willow tree is due to be pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: osiers are willows regularly cut back for their rods.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a species of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basketwork.

clue.text: Study child actress

blocks.note: a den is a private study
ch is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: Someone is studying a young performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb; it is the noun for a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Judi Dench is a celebrated English stage and screen actress.

clue.text: Introduces new members

definitions.note: noun plural, while the first definition is a verb

blocks.note: first meaning, a verb: starts off or admits
second meaning, a noun: people recently admitted to a group

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about introducing newcomers, but splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to begin or induct someone, and initiates are novices just admitted to a society.
